clue.text: Denied being featured apart from a broadcast

indicators.note: apart from means except, so the single letter named next is left out of the word before it
something broadcast is scattered widely, so the remaining letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone protests they never appeared in a broadcast programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To refute a claim is to reject or contradict it, so the past tense matches denied.

clue.text: Religious figure meets another over talks

definitions.note: a verb: rabbits on, chatters at length, so third person singular matches

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upward, so the second religious figure is written backwards
meets means comes up against, so one figure is simply placed next to the other

blocks.note: another religious figure: a saint, abbreviated

explanation.surface: Two clergymen meeting for a summit of interfaith talks.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit, or rabbit on, is British slang for chattering endlessly, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' for talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbits is informal British for chatters on at length, the same as talks in the sense of speaking a lot.

clue.text: How to give up one's yen for shekels?

definitions.text: How to give up one's yen for shekels?

blocks.clueFragment: How to give up one's yen
blocks.note: surface reading: how to abandon a longing or craving
setter's reading: yen and shekels are the currencies of Japan and Israel, and swapping one for the other is a currency trade

explanation.walkthrough: A yen is a yearning, and having a yen for money sounds like greed; but yen is also Japanese money, traded here for Israeli shekels.
explanation.definitionFit: Converting one country's money into another country's money is a transaction in the international currency market.

clue.text: What helps make concert a hit? I answer, 'Folk coming from afar'

indicators.note: what helps make a phrase is a part of it, so letters are lifted from inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: runs across concerT A HIT I, ignoring the punctuation

explanation.surface: A musician explaining that a concert's success comes from performers who travelled a long way.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is an island in French Polynesia in the South Pacific, so its people come from a very distant place for most solvers.

clue.text: Rough behind - get doctor onto that

definitions.note: a noun here, as an artist's rough is a first sketch, matching the noun draft

indicators.note: in a down clue putting one thing onto another places it on top, so it comes first

blocks.note: aft means at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone with a sore backside told to get a doctor to look at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough behind' reads as a sore bottom, but 'Rough' is the definition and 'behind' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A preliminary version of a document or design is called both a rough and a draft.

clue.text: Occasions for politicians to take time

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so the politicians enclose the letter for time

explanation.surface: Political occasions on which members of parliament are given time to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasions' reads as a plural noun, but it is the verb: to occasion something is to cause it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to cause or bring about, as when an event prompts a reaction.

clue.text: Little dog, favourite always in the old days for Punch and Judy man?

blocks.note: a teacher's pet is a favourite
e'er, the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: A seaside showman whose little dog Toby has always been the audience favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch and Judy is a traditional British seaside show with hand puppets; the dog Toby is one of its characters.
explanation.definitionFit: Punch and Judy shows are performed with glove puppets, so the man running one is a puppet operator; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Revolutionary vicar that's wearing to public

indicators.note: a wearer is inside the clothing, so the vicar sits within the little word that follows
revolutionary means turning right over, so the whole combination is read backwards

blocks.note: short for Reverend, a vicar's title

explanation.surface: A radical clergyman whose views are gradually wearing down the public.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overt is done openly and in plain sight, so it is public rather than hidden.

clue.text: Journalists questioning printer's base fee - concern spreading

indicators.note: spreading out loosens the order, so the letters before it are laid out afresh

blocks.note: a printing press is the machine a printer works with

explanation.surface: Reporters grilling a printing firm about worries over its rising basic charges.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting called so that reporters can put questions to someone is an occasion of journalists questioning.

clue.text: Gathered Independent's forty, vacant and content

definitions.note: a verb here, to make someone content, matching the verb

indicators.note: vacant means emptied, so only the outside letters of the number remain

blocks.note: a committee sat, meaning it met or gathered
I for Independent, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: An independent politician turned forty, empty-headed but happy with life.
explanation.definitionFit: To content someone is to please or gratify them, which is what satisfy means as a verb.

clue.text: We get this annually readjusted by a third here

indicators.note: readjusted means set up afresh, so the letters of the words that follow are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Something, perhaps a salary, adjusted upward by a third each year.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift received once every year on the anniversary of being born fits a cryptic description of something got annually.

clue.text: I had X - Twitter - originally displayed as 'Twit'

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: I'd, the contraction of I had
X is the Roman numeral ten, written as 10, which looks like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A user of X, formerly Twitter, shown up as a twit.
explanation.walkthrough: The social network X was once called Twitter; here X just means the number ten, drawn with letter shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: A twit is a silly, foolish person, an everyday synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Collection of essays, maybe half of that is restricted by elders?

definitions.note: a plural answer for a collection: several formal essays

indicators.note: half of keeps only two of the four letters in the word that comes next
something restricted is hemmed in, so these letters sit inside the trees
maybe flags that the elders are an example of a wider class of thing

blocks.note: elders are a kind of tree
the second half of the word

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a book of essays is being censored by the older generation.
explanation.walkthrough: Elders look like senior people, but they are elder trees, hence 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a long formal written discussion of a subject, so several make up a collection of essays.

clue.text: Place filling shavings in gap or eaves

indicators.note: filling is what is packed inside, so the answer lies within the run of words that follows

blocks.note: runs across the words shavingS IN GAP OR Eaves

explanation.surface: A builder stuffing wood shavings into a gap or the eaves of a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: The city-state in Southeast Asia is a geographical place, here defined as broadly as possible.

clue.text: Official investigator getting over maiden shoots staff

blocks.note: O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
M is a maiden over in cricket scoring
buds are young shoots on a plant
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: An inspector investigating a girl who shot members of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is six balls and a maiden is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman is appointed to look into complaints against public bodies or companies, an official role of inquiry.

clue.text: Loud Yankee goes round excessively backing 'soccer'

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word for excessively is read from its end
to go round something is to surround it, so the loud and Yankee letters enclose the rest

blocks.note: Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A noisy American fan cheering soccer far too enthusiastically.
explanation.definitionFit: Footy is British slang for football, which Americans call soccer.

clue.text: Nice guys?

blocks.note: setter's reading: Nice is a city on the Riviera, so men from Nice are natives of that country

explanation.walkthrough: The capital letter on 'Nice' is hidden by its place at the start of the clue; read it as the French city, pronounced 'neece'.
explanation.definitionFit: Men from the Riviera city are male citizens of the country it belongs to, of which they are examples.

clue.text: Misleads rivals with boarding times

indicators.note: boarding means getting aboard, so the multiplication sign gets inside the enemies

explanation.surface: A sneaky competitor fooling opponents with fake boarding times at an airport.
explanation.definitionFit: To fox someone is to baffle or deceive them, so foxes and misleads are verb synonyms.

clue.text: Huts for frolicking - unusual quarters!

indicators.note: frolicking means romping about wildly, so the letters jump into a different order

explanation.surface: Holiday huts set aside for fun make strange lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' looks like lodgings, matching the huts, but it means divisions into four.
explanation.definitionFit: A fourth and a quarter are both one of four equal parts, but fourths is the rarer word in British use, hence unusual.

clue.text: Typically boozy load rub ref all the wrong way

indicators.note: doing something the wrong way gets it out of order, so these letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunken load of fans rubbing the referee up the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: A cask filled to capacity usually holds beer or wine, so the amount it contains is a load of booze.

clue.text: Flipping 'no' then 'yes' from the Spanish - pain working together

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the whole string of pieces is read backwards

blocks.note: to ail is to cause pain

explanation.surface: Someone switching from no to yes in Spanish, painfully indecisive.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a close working relationship or cooperation between people or groups, so it is a form of collaboration.

clue.text: International group leader saving king from revolutionary

indicators.note: saving means keeping safe, so the leader holds the king within

blocks.note: of can mean from, as in a man of Kent

explanation.surface: A UN chief rescuing a monarch from a revolutionary uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a rebel, but it is the definition in its sense of utterly new.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unheard-of has never happened before, so it is novel and groundbreaking in the way a revolutionary idea is.

clue.text: A lot to be seen going over France in the air

indicators.note: going over something can mean covering it, so the phrase before is wrapped around the country

blocks.note: the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: Many planes visible flying over France.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloft means high up, overhead or in flight, so an adverb meaning up in the sky.

clue.text: Organisers of 14 Across engaging in large Wembley event?

indicators.note: engaging means drawing in or occupying, so the organisers hold the little word within

blocks.note: the Football Association runs English football

explanation.surface: The football authorities getting involved in a big event at Wembley.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 Across is FOOTY, football; Wembley is the London stadium where English cup finals are played.
explanation.definitionFit: The deciding match of a competition such as the FA Cup is held at Wembley, an example signalled by the question mark.

clue.text: Regularly highlighted dancer disco revolved around

indicators.note: regularly highlighted means picked out at even intervals, so every second letter is taken
revolved means turned round, so the chosen letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A spotlit dancer twirling about in a disco.
explanation.definitionFit: Circa is Latin used in English before dates and figures to mean approximately, the same as around.

clue.text: Charge fellows in teepees for mystical tablets?

indicators.note: in places the charge and the fellows inside the word for teepees

blocks.note: to charge someone with doing something is to command it

explanation.surface: Charging people money to camp in teepees, like some New Age retreat selling mystical goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Moses received the laws from God carved on stone tablets, so they are divine, sacred tablets.

clue.text: On reflection, web's hosting little that's mellow

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the other way round, so the word for web's is written backwards
a host has guests inside, so the backwards word holds the little one

explanation.surface: Musing that the internet contains a few things that are soothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweeten is to make gentler or more agreeable, as to mellow a mood or flavour.

clue.text: Light way to lead Navy across Dart's east bank

indicators.note: lying across something spans it, so the way is stretched around the next letter
on a map east is on the right, so the east bank of a word is its final letter
to lead means to go in front, so the way comes before the navy

blocks.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A lamp guiding the navy across to the east bank of the river Dart in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dart is a river in Devon, home of the naval college at Dartmouth, so the scene is real; only its final letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp in a case, a common kind of light.
